steps.instruction: Pick a paired-data dataset (each row is a matched pair: same subject before/after, twin pairs, matched cases and controls, etc.). Confirm the data are truly paired before continuing.
steps.observe: What is the parameter of interest here - a single mean, a difference of two independent means, or the mean of the WITHIN-pair differences?
steps.reveal: The parameter is mu_D, the mean of the within-pair differences (e.g., mean of after_i - before_i). Analyzing paired data as if it were two independent groups throws away the pairing and inflates the standard error.

steps.instruction: The tool computes the differences D_i = value2_i - value1_i automatically. Look at the displayed distribution of D_i.
steps.observe: Does the distribution of DIFFERENCES look roughly symmetric? Any outliers? What matters for the paired t is the distribution of D, not the two originals.
steps.reveal: Only the distribution of the DIFFERENCES needs to look approximately normal (or n large enough for CLT). The two original distributions can be wildly skewed and the paired t still works - as long as the differences are well-behaved.

steps.instruction: Run the paired t-test with a two-sided alternative. Read off t, df = n - 1, and the p-value.
steps.observe: What is your decision at alpha = 0.05? Does the 95% CI for mu_D exclude 0?
steps.reveal: At alpha = 0.05 reject H0 iff p < 0.05. Rejecting H0 means the mean within-pair difference is discernibly non-zero - the two conditions (before/after, treatment/control-within-twin) genuinely produce different mean outcomes.

steps.instruction: Now analyze the SAME numbers in /inference/two-means/ as if they were two independent groups. Compare the two p-values and the two 95% CIs.
steps.observe: Which CI is wider? Which p-value is smaller? What did the pairing buy you?
steps.reveal: The paired analysis is dramatically more powerful when subjects are their own controls - the within-subject variability is much smaller than between-subject variability. Ignoring the pairing (using two-sample t) is 'throwing away information': same data, wider CI, larger p, less power. This is why paired designs are worth the extra effort.

steps.instruction: Write a one-sentence conclusion in context. Address whether the interpretation is CAUSAL (if the pairs were randomly assigned) or merely ASSOCIATIONAL.
steps.observe: Was the pairing achieved by random assignment (e.g., a within-subject randomized study) or by matching on observed characteristics?
steps.reveal: Random assignment within pairs supports a causal reading (the within-pair difference isolates the treatment effect). Observed matching only controls for the variables you matched on; unmeasured confounders can still create associations without causation.
